clue.text: But it's working in the theatre

definitions.text: But it's working in the theatre

parts.words: But it's working in the theatre
parts.note: on stage, actors at their job are said to be doing something that elsewhere sounds like leisure, not labour

explanation.surface: A wry remark that what looks like idleness counts as a job on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors who perform a show are at work, yet the word for what they do also means amusing oneself.

clue.text: Yes, pale gets split up in the battle

indicators.note: split up says the letters of the fodder are broken apart and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder as the setter meant it, Yes, pals, with the printed pale one letter off

explanation.surface: Friends agreeing to part on the field of conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, YES PALE has two Es and one S; the clue must have read 'Yes, pals get split up', an anagram of YES PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive's 1757 victory in Bengal was fought at this place, so the name stands for the battle.

clue.text: Roads to town

explanation.surface: Directions on how to reach a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads (as in Hampton Roads) are sheltered water for ships to anchor; the largest city of Alaska also bears the name.

clue.text: "Say that Creator made from designs by Michael Angelo!" (Mark Twain)

definitions.text: "Say that Creator made from designs by Michael Angelo!" (Mark Twain)

parts.words: "Say that Creator made from designs by Michael Angelo!" (Mark Twain)
parts.note: a quotation from The Innocents Abroad with its country removed, the place Twain mocked for crediting Michelangelo with everything

explanation.surface: A gap-fill quotation from Mark Twain's travel satire.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a dash where the missing country goes; Twain's guide credited Michelangelo with everything in that land.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain's line jokes that the whole Renaissance homeland of Michelangelo was his creation.

clue.text: Waterman possibly singing "Barcarolle'"?

parts.note: a barcarolle is the song of a Venetian boatman, and Gilbert and Sullivan named an opera after such boatmen

explanation.surface: Picturing a boatman crooning a Venetian song.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian boatman who poles a canal craft traditionally sings barcarolles.

clue.text: Writers of lines about set-back

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the old UK railway lines
on means about, concerning

indicators.note: back tells us the word set is read the other way round

explanation.surface: Authors of verse write about a setback they suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' looks like one noun, but 'back' turns SET into TES after BR (British Rail) and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, Emily and Anne of that surname were the famous novelist sisters.

clue.text: Good sort of building material

explanation.surface: A decent kind of material for building.
explanation.definitionFit: A reliable, helpful friend is called a brick; fired clay blocks are a building material.

clue.text: Sound rude when doctor and scholar interrupt complaints investigator

indicators.note: interrupt says the degrees break into the reworked letters
when the doctor is placed, it goes within the reworked word
rude means rough or unpolished, telling us the word sound is roughly reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the word to be rearranged
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
MA is Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: Sounding off rudely as a doctor and academic cut in on an official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' rearranges SOUND to O-UDS-N; MB goes after the O and MA after the S. 'Sound rude' reads as a verb phrase, but it is fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: An official appointed to look into public grievances against institutions.

clue.text: Chipolata upended, not wholly brownish-grey

indicators.note: not wholly says the answer is a run inside the words, not all of them

explanation.surface: A sausage tipped over, part-eaten and grey-brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upended' looks like a reversal sign in a down clue, but the run is read forwards; it is just part of the hiding text.
explanation.definitionFit: Taupe is a moleskin colour between brown and grey.

clue.text: So Rachel's distressed after loss of oriental savant

indicators.note: distressed means upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order
after loss of says a letter is dropped from the words before they are scrambled

parts.note: Rachel's stands for 'Rachel is', so only the name gives letters
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: So Rachel is upset after losing a learned Eastern sage.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person, an academic expert, is a savant.

clue.text: A cricket club run by a place in Ghana

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket club is managed by someone from a West African town.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Ghana is a place there.

clue.text: Cleaner needed to fix electric conductor

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
a brush is the carbon contact that conducts current in a motor or dynamo

explanation.surface: An electrician's job: you need a cleaner to fix the wiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stiff brush for scrubbing fingernails is a cleaning tool.

clue.text: Such a happy ending for work by leading southern politician

indicators.note: by means the work stands beside, next after, what precedes it
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: S for southern, placed in the leading position
a Tory is a British Conservative politician
a book is a written work

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale finish for a book by a prominent politician from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale conclusion where all ends well is often called a storybook finish.

clue.text: Live and prosper, losing nothing

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the two-word phrase for prosper

parts.note: to do well is to prosper
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A take on the blessing 'live long and prosper', minus something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing nothing' looks like 'without loss', but it removes O from DO WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to make one's home or abode there.

clue.text: It may cause a rising from an unknown quarter

parts.note: Y is an unknown in algebra
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A rebellion breaks out somewhere in a distant, unidentified region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suggests a revolt; it is dough swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus added to bread makes dough swell by producing gas.

clue.text: Times for Thor

explanation.surface: A newspaper name for the god of thunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times of London was nicknamed The Thunderer in the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times newspaper's old nickname also describes the Norse god who wields thunderbolts.

clue.text: He hints at alternative form of matin rite

indicators.note: an alternative form of the words means their letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman suggests a different version of the morning service.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who suggests things indirectly is one who insinuates.

clue.text: Shed in poorly rated Yorkshire town

indicators.note: in places the synonym inside the jumbled letters
poorly means badly, so the word rated is jumbled

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake its skin

explanation.surface: A garden shed in a badly regarded northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' makes TADER from RATED, and CAST goes between TAD and ER. TADCASTER is a brewing town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in North Yorkshire known for its breweries.

clue.text: Mournful but rich-toned arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means they are reordered

explanation.surface: A sad yet richly voiced musical arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament for the dead, so the adjective means mournful.

clue.text: Kind of career for a draughtsman?

definitions.text: Kind of career for a draughtsman?

parts.words: Kind of career for a draughtsman?
parts.note: a draughts player works on a board of squares in two colours, and a career of ups and downs has the same adjective

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of working life suits a technical drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: A draughtsman here is a player of draughts, the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A career with mixed fortunes is described by the same word as a board marked in squares.

clue.text: Grumbling at the little noise we hear when driving

definitions.text: the little noise we hear when driving

explanation.surface: Complaining about a small sound from the engine on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as CAR PING, a small knocking noise from a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty fault-finding is nagging criticism; split, the word is a ping heard from a car.

clue.text: Shark may be tender

explanation.surface: A predator of the sea might prove gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse shark is a bottom-dwelling species; a carer who tends patients is also so called.

clue.text: Incessant in the city of Rome, for example

definitions.text: the city of Rome, for example

explanation.surface: Something unending in the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Never-ending things are everlasting; Rome is called the Eternal City.

clue.text: Mad artist with a proposition

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a bid is an offer or proposition

explanation.surface: A crazy painter comes with a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious or fanatical, as in a frenzied supporter.

clue.text: Continue the innings — stick in there

explanation.surface: A cricketer told to keep batting and hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket to bat on is to keep batting; split, the phrase also names a stick such as a conductor's or relay runner's.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping on batting in cricket; a short rod passed in relays or waved by a conductor.

clue.text: Dare to differ about retrograde measure

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the other

parts.note: to change is to become different

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the measure is read in reverse

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure

explanation.surface: Daring to disagree about a backward step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrograde' turns ELL into LLE, which sits inside CHANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to defy them to do something.

clue.text: Basket of fish given to King Charles

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles's royal cipher
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A hamper of fish presented to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker container for carrying the catch.

clue.text: Student at university free to become sensational

parts.note: L is the learner plate, a student driver
U is short for university
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A college student, newly liberated, becomes headline news.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking, garish reporting is described as gaudy or melodramatic.

clue.text: Cut across to put down a religious faction

parts.note: to inter is to put down in the grave, bury
a sect is a religious faction

explanation.surface: Breaking across to suppress a breakaway church group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that meet and pass through one another cross each other.

clue.text: Element of trouble in its symbol

indicators.note: in places the trouble within the symbol

parts.note: Rn is the chemical symbol of this gas
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A hint of difficulty in some emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive noble gas is a chemical element, number 86.

clue.text: Grant, for instance, is not particular

explanation.surface: A man named Grant isn't fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant was a US Civil War commander; something broad and non-specific is also so described.

clue.text: Fundamental sign of mathematics

explanation.surface: A basic symbol in maths.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic or root-level things are so described; the root sign in maths has the same name.
